3 days in Lisbon: Alfama first, Belém second, the flat grid last.
A walking itinerary if you sleep in the centre. The tram is a ride through streets you can also walk. Sintra, Cascais and Évora are each their own day — not an extra on day 3.
Lisbon and the Tagus seen from Castelo de São Jorge toward Praça do Comércio
Day 1 — Alfama, one miradouro, and the tram only if a seat is empty
Start at the Sé and walk up to Largo das Portas do Sol and Miradouro de Santa Luzia. The view over the roofs is free.
Keep climbing to Miradouro da Senhora do Monte if you want the whole city in one glance. It is a hill, not a taxi problem, unless your knees say otherwise.

Tram 28E is a Carris tram from Martim Moniz to Campo de Ourique (Prazeres), through Graça, Santa Luzia, the Sé and Chiado. It does not go to Belém. The queue is at the first stop. Walk the same streets, or board further along when a seat is actually empty.

Day 2 — Belém, and only the ticket you will actually use
Train from Cais do Sodré on the Cascais line. On CP’s urban timetable a midday departure at 10:40 from Cais do Sodré is timed into Belém at 10:48. Check
the Cascais-line timetable
the morning you go.
Or tram 15E, Praça da Figueira to Algés, which stops at Belém (Museu dos Coches) and the Centro Cultural de Belém.
Carris 15E
Jerónimos cloister if the slot is already yours. Belém Tower from the river walk if it is not. Doing both interiors on a hot afternoon is how the day disappears.

Day 3 — Baixa and Chiado, then one extra, not three
Rossio, Rua Augusta, Praça do Comércio. This is the flat part of the city, which is the point after two days of hills.
Chiado in the late afternoon. The Santa Justa lift is a queue for a view you can also get from the Carmo terrace beside it.
Either LX Factory in Alcântara — shops under the 25 de Abril bridge, not a morning monument — or a sunset back at a miradouro. Not both, and not Sintra on top.
